sanskrit: tam ṛte phalgunaṃ vīraṃ na labhe kāmyake dhṛtim śūnyām iva ca paśyāmi tatra tatra mahīm imām
english: Without that hero Phalguna I find no peace of mind in Kāmyaka; wherever I look, this earth seems to me empty and void.

sanskrit: nakula uvāca ya udīcīṃ diśaṃ gatvā jitvā yudhi mahābalān gandharvamukhyāñ śataśo hayāṃl lebhe sa vāsaviḥ
english: Nakula said: He who journeyed to the northern region and, conquering in battle mighty foes — the leading Gandharvas by the hundreds — obtained horses, that son of Vāsava —

sanskrit: rājaṃs tittirikalmāṣāñ śrīmān anilaraṃhasaḥ prādād bhrātre priyaḥ premṇā rājasūye mahākratau
english: O king, the glorious one swift as the wind — in his love he gladly gave those tittiri-spotted steeds to his brother at the great Rājasūya sacrifice —

sanskrit: tam ṛte bhīmadhanvānaṃ bhīmād avarajaṃ vane kāmaye kāmyake vāsaṃ nedānīm amaropamam
english: Without him, the terrible-bowed younger brother of Bhīma, I have no desire to dwell in the Kāmyaka forest, which now seems to me no heaven at all.

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca yo dhanāni ca kanyāś ca yudhi jitvā mahārathān ājahāra purā rājñe rājasūye mahākratau
english: Sahadeva said: He who, having conquered great warriors in battle, formerly brought home both riches and maidens for the king at the great Rājasūya sacrifice —

sanskrit: yaḥ sametān mṛdhe jitvā yādavān amitadyutiḥ subhadrām ājahāraiko vāsudevasya saṃmate
english: He of immeasurable splendour who, single-handedly defeating the assembled Yādavas in battle, carried off Subhadrā with Vāsudeva's approval —

sanskrit: tasya jiṣṇor bṛsīṃ dṛṣṭvā śūnyām upaniveśane hṛdayaṃ me mahārāja na śāmyati kadā cana
english: Seeing the seat of that Jiṣṇu empty in our encampment, my heart, O great king, cannot find peace at any time.

sanskrit: vanād asmād vivāsaṃ tu rocaye 'ham ariṃdama na hi nas tam ṛte vīraṃ ramaṇīyam idaṃ vanam
english: O crusher of foes, I have a mind to leave this forest; for without that hero, this forest holds no delight for us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhanaṃjayotsukās te tu vane tasmin mahārathāḥ nyavasanta mahābhāgā draupadyā saha pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yearning for Dhanañjaya, those great warriors the Pāṇḍavas of great fortune, together with Draupadī, dwelt in that forest.

sanskrit: athāpaśyan mahātmānaṃ devarṣiṃ tatra nāradam dīpyamānaṃ śriyā brāhmyā dīptāgnisamatejasam
english: Then they beheld there the great-souled divine seer Nārada, blazing with the splendour of Brahmā, brilliant as a kindled fire.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śrīmān bhrātṛbhiḥ kurusattamaḥ vibabhāv atidīptaujā devair iva śatakratuḥ
english: The glorious foremost of the Kurus, surrounded by those brothers, shone with surpassing radiant energy, even as Śatakratu surrounded by the gods.

sanskrit: yathā ca vedān sāvitrī yājñasenī tathā satī na jahau dharmataḥ pārthān merum arkaprabhā yathā
english: And just as the Sāvitrī does not abandon the Vedas, so the chaste Yājñasenī never abandoned the Pārthas from righteousness, even as the sun-bright Śrī does not desert Mount Meru.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ āśvāsayad dharmasutaṃ yuktarūpam ivānagha
english: Receiving that worship, the blessed seer Nārada comforted the son of Dharma with words fitly spoken, O sinless one.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahātmānaṃ dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram brūhi dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha kenārthaḥ kiṃ dadāmi te
english: And he spoke to the great-souled Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira: "Speak, O foremost of the upholders of righteousness — what purpose do you have, and what shall I give you?"

sanskrit: atha dharmasuto rājā praṇamya bhrātṛbhiḥ saha uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ nāradaṃ devasaṃmitam
english: Then the king, son of Dharma, having bowed together with his brothers, spoke with joined palms to Nārada, who is comparable to the gods.

sanskrit: tvayi tuṣṭe mahābhāga sarvalokābhipūjite kṛtam ity eva manye 'haṃ prasādāt tava suvrata
english: "When you are pleased, O greatly fortunate one, worshipped by all the worlds, I consider my purpose accomplished by your grace, O one of excellent vows.

sanskrit: yadi tv aham anugrāhyo bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nagha saṃdehaṃ me muniśreṣṭha hṛdisthaṃ chettum arhasi
english: Yet if I, together with my brothers, am worthy of your favour, O sinless one, O best of sages, please be pleased to resolve the doubt that dwells in my heart.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ yaḥ kurute pṛthivīṃ tīrthatatparaḥ kiṃ phalaṃ tasya kārtsnyena tad brahman vaktum arhasi
english: He who circumambulates the earth, devoted to holy places of pilgrimage — what is the full fruit of that? O Brahman, please tell it to me in its entirety."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śṛṇu rājann avahito yathā bhīṣmeṇa bhārata pulastyasya sakāśād vai sarvam etad upaśrutam
english: Nārada said: "Listen attentively, O king, O Bhārata — all this was heard by Bhīṣma himself from the presence of Pulastya; hear it as he received it.

sanskrit: purā bhāgīrathītīre bhīṣmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ pitryaṃ vrataṃ samāsthāya nyavasan munivat tadā
english: Long ago on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, Bhīṣma, best of the upholders of righteousness, having undertaken the ancestral vow, dwelt there at that time like a sage.

sanskrit: śubhe deśe mahārāja puṇye devarṣisevite gaṅgādvāre mahātejā devagandharvasevite
english: In an auspicious place, O great king, a holy site frequented by divine sages — at the gate of the Gaṅgā, that mighty one of great energy, frequented by gods and gandharvas.

sanskrit: sa pitṝṃs tarpayām āsa devāṃś ca paramadyutiḥ ṛṣīṃś ca toṣayām āsa vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: He of supreme brilliance satisfied the ancestors and the gods, and pleased the sages with actions prescribed by sacred ordinance.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya japann eva mahātapāḥ dadarśādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ pulastyam ṛṣisattamam
english: Then after some time, while engaged in reciting prayers, that great ascetic beheld the seer Pulastya, best among sages, wondrous in appearance.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvogratapasaṃ dīpyamānam iva śriyā praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe vismayaṃ ca paraṃ yayau
english: Seeing him who was fierce in austerity and blazing as it were with splendour, he was filled with incomparable joy and overcome with the greatest wonder.

sanskrit: upasthitaṃ mahārāja pūjayām āsa bhārata bhīṣmo dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Bhīṣma, best of the upholders of righteousness, when he had appeared before him, O great king, O Bhārata, honoured him with actions prescribed by sacred ordinance.

sanskrit: śirasā cārghyam ādāya śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ nāma saṃkīrtayām āsa tasmin brahmarṣisattame
english: With pure body and composed mind, he took the honorific offering with his head bowed and announced his name to that best of brahmin seers.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo 'ham asmi bhadraṃ te dāso 'smi tava suvrata tava saṃdarśanād eva mukto 'haṃ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
english: "I am Bhīṣma — blessings to you; I am your servant, O one of excellent vows; by the very sight of you I am freed from all sins."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja bhīṣmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ vāgyataḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā tūṣṇīm āsīd yudhiṣṭhira
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, O Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, best of the upholders of righteousness, controlled his speech, folded his hands, and fell silent.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā niyamenātha svādhyāyāmnāyakarśitam bhīṣmaṃ kurukulaśreṣṭhaṃ muniḥ prītamanābhavat
english: Seeing him, that best of the Kuru lineage, Bhīṣma, thus disciplined and emaciated by recitation and scriptural study, the sage became filled with affection.

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca anena tava dharmajña praśrayeṇa damena ca satyena ca mahābhāga tuṣṭo 'smi tava sarvaśaḥ
english: Pulastya said: "By this humility of yours, O knower of righteousness, and by your self-restraint and truthfulness, O greatly fortunate one, I am entirely pleased with you.

sanskrit: yasyedṛśas te dharmo 'yaṃ pitṛbhaktyāśrito 'nagha tena paśyasi māṃ putra prītiś cāpi mama tvayi
english: Because of this righteousness of yours, rooted in devotion to your father, O sinless one, you behold me, my son; and my affection too is yours.

sanskrit: amoghadarśī bhīṣmāhaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te yad vakṣyasi kuruśreṣṭha tasya dātāsmi te 'nagha
english: O Bhīṣma, I am one whose sight does not go in vain — tell me, what shall I do for you? Whatever you shall say, O best of the Kurus, that I shall give you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca prīte tvayi mahābhāga sarvalokābhipūjite kṛtam ity eva manye 'haṃ yad ahaṃ dṛṣṭavān prabhum
english: Bhīṣma said: "When you are pleased, O greatly fortunate one worshipped by all the worlds, I count it accomplished — that I have beheld the lord.

sanskrit: yadi tv aham anugrāhyas tava dharmabhṛtāṃ vara vakṣyāmi hṛtsthaṃ saṃdehaṃ tan me tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: Yet if I am worthy of your favour, O best of the upholders of righteousness, I shall state the doubt that lodges in my heart — and please be pleased to resolve it for me.

sanskrit: asti me bhagavan kaś cit tīrthebhyo dharmasaṃśayaḥ tam ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi pṛthak saṃkīrtitaṃ tvayā
english: O blessed one, I have a certain question about righteousness concerning sacred pilgrimages; I desire to hear it explained by you one by one.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ yaḥ pṛthivīṃ karoty amitavikrama kiṃ phalaṃ tasya viprarṣe tan me brūhi tapodhana
english: He who circumambulates the earth, O sage among brahmins, O treasury of austerity — what is the fruit of that? Tell me this, O man of immeasurable might."

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca hanta te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi yad ṛṣīṇāṃ parāyaṇam tad ekāgramanās tāta śṛṇu tīrtheṣu yat phalam
english: Pulastya said: "Well then, I shall tell you what is the highest resort of the sages — with mind focused, my dear, hear what the fruit is in holy places of pilgrimage.

sanskrit: yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaś caiva susaṃyatam vidyā tapaś ca kīrtiś ca sa tīrthaphalam aśnute
english: He whose hands and feet and mind are well controlled, and who possesses learning, austerity, and fame — he enjoys the fruit of a pilgrimage to holy places.

sanskrit: pratigrahād upāvṛttaḥ saṃtuṣṭo niyataḥ śuciḥ ahaṃkāranivṛttaś ca sa tīrthaphalam aśnute
english: He who has withdrawn from accepting gifts, who is contented, disciplined, pure, and free from ego — he enjoys the fruit of a pilgrimage to holy places.

sanskrit: akalkako nirārambho laghv āhāro jitendriyaḥ vimuktaḥ sarvadoṣair yaḥ sa tīrthaphalam aśnute
english: He who is free from deceit, free from worldly undertakings, light in eating, master of his senses, and released from all faults — he enjoys the fruit of a pilgrimage to holy places.

sanskrit: akrodhanaś ca rājendra satyaśīlo dṛḍhavrataḥ ātmopamaś ca bhūteṣu sa tīrthaphalam aśnute
english: He who is free from anger, O king of kings, whose nature is truthfulness, whose vows are firm, and who regards all beings as equal to himself — he enjoys the fruit of a pilgrimage to holy places.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ kratavaḥ proktā vedeṣv iha yathākramam phalaṃ caiva yathātattvaṃ pretya ceha ca sarvaśaḥ
english: The sages have declared sacrifices in the Vedas in proper order, with their fruit exactly as it is, both in the hereafter and in this world, in every respect.

sanskrit: na te śakyā daridreṇa yajñāḥ prāptuṃ mahīpate bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsaṃbhāravistarāḥ
english: Those sacrifices cannot be performed by one who is poor, O lord of the earth; sacrifices require many instruments and a vast array of various materials.

sanskrit: prāpyante pārthivair ete samṛddhair vā naraiḥ kva cit nārthanyūnopakaraṇair ekātmabhir asaṃhataiḥ
english: These are accessible to kings or to wealthy men somewhere; but not to those deficient in means and equipment, who are isolated and unsupported.

sanskrit: yo daridrair api vidhiḥ śakyaḥ prāptuṃ nareśvara tulyo yajñaphalaiḥ puṇyais taṃ nibodha yudhāṃ vara
english: O lord of men, O best of warriors, learn then of that practice which even the poor can accomplish and which equals the merit of sacrifices in its holy fruit.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ paramaṃ guhyam idaṃ bharatasattama tīrthābhigamanaṃ puṇyaṃ yajñair api viśiṣyate
english: This is the supreme secret of the sages, O best of the Bhāratas — the holy act of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites excels even sacrifices.

sanskrit: anupoṣya trirātrāṇi tīrthāny anabhigamya ca adattvā kāñcanaṃ gāś ca daridro nāma jāyate
english: Not fasting for three nights, not visiting holy places, not giving gold and cows — through these omissions one is born poor.

sanskrit: agniṣṭomādibhir yajñair iṣṭvā vipuladakṣiṇaiḥ na tat phalam avāpnoti tīrthābhigamanena yat
english: Having performed sacrifices like the Agniṣṭoma with generous sacrificial fees, one does not obtain that fruit which comes from visiting holy places of pilgrimage.

sanskrit: nṛloke devadevasya tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam puṣkaraṃ nāma vikhyātaṃ mahābhāgaḥ samāviśet
english: In the world of men, the holy place of the god of gods, famous throughout the three worlds, known as Puṣkara — a fortunate man should enter it.

sanskrit: daśa koṭisahasrāṇi tīrthānāṃ vai mahīpate sāṃnidhyaṃ puṣkare yeṣāṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ kurunandana
english: Ten thousand crores of holy places are present at Puṣkara, O lord of the earth, at the three twilight junctions of day, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyāś ca samarudgaṇāḥ gandharvāpsarasaś caiva nityaṃ saṃnihitā vibho
english: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, and the Marut hosts, as well as the Gandharvas and Apsarases, are always present there, O lord.

sanskrit: yatra devās tapas taptvā daityā brahmarṣayas tathā divyayogā mahārāja puṇyena mahatānvitāḥ
english: Where the gods, the Daityas, and the brahmin sages as well, endowed with divine yoga and possessed of great merit, performed austerities, O great king.

sanskrit: manasāpy abhikāmasya puṣkarāṇi manasvinaḥ pūyante sarvapāpāni nākapṛṣṭhe ca pūjyate
english: Even for the wise man who desires Puṣkara only in mind, all sins are purified, and he is honoured on the back of heaven.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthe mahābhāga nityam eva pitāmahaḥ uvāsa paramaprīto devadānavasaṃmataḥ
english: At that holy place, O greatly fortunate one, the Grandfather himself ever dwelt, supremely pleased, revered by gods and Dānavas alike.

sanskrit: puṣkareṣu mahābhāga devāḥ sarṣipurogamāḥ siddhiṃ samabhisaṃprāptāḥ puṇyena mahatānvitāḥ
english: At Puṣkara, O greatly fortunate one, the gods together with the leading sages attained perfection, endowed as they were with great merit.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt pitṛdevārcane rataḥ aśvamedhaṃ daśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: He who bathes there while devoted to honouring ancestors and gods — the wise declare it ten times the equal of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: apy ekaṃ bhojayed vipraṃ puṣkarāraṇyam āśritaḥ tenāsau karmaṇā bhīṣma pretya ceha ca modate
english: Even if one feeds a single brahmin while dwelling in the Puṣkara forest, by that act, O Bhīṣma, he rejoices both in the hereafter and in this world.

sanskrit: śākamūlaphalair vāpi yena vartayate svayam tad vai dadyād brāhmaṇāya śraddhāvān anasūyakaḥ tenaiva prāpnuyāt prājño hayamedhaphalaṃ naraḥ
english: Or whoever sustains himself on vegetables, roots, and fruits — if he, faithful and free from envy, gives even that to a brahmin, by that very act the wise man attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro vā rājasattama na viyoniṃ vrajanty ete snātās tīrthe mahātmanaḥ
english: Whether a brahmin, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra, O best of kings — those who bathe at the holy place of that great soul do not go to a degraded birth.

sanskrit: kārttikyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa yo 'bhigaccheta puṣkaram phalaṃ tatrākṣayaṃ tasya vardhate bharatarṣabha
english: But he who comes to Puṣkara especially on the full moon of Kārttika — his fruit there grows without limit, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ prātaḥ smared yas tu puṣkarāṇi kṛtāñjaliḥ upaspṛṣṭaṃ bhavet tena sarvatīrtheṣu bhārata prāpnuyāc ca naro lokān brahmaṇaḥ sadane 'kṣayān
english: He who remembers Puṣkara morning and evening with joined palms — it is as though he has touched all holy places, O Bhārata; and that man attains the imperishable worlds in the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti yat pāpaṃ striyo vā puruṣasya vā puṣkare snātamātrasya sarvam eva praṇaśyati
english: Whatever sin has accumulated since birth — whether of a woman or a man — all of it perishes completely for one who has merely bathed at Puṣkara.

sanskrit: yathā surāṇāṃ sarveṣām ādis tu madhusūdanaḥ tathaiva puṣkaraṃ rājaṃs tīrthānām ādir ucyate
english: Just as Madhusūdana is declared the first among all the gods, so too, O king, Puṣkara is declared the first among all holy places.

sanskrit: uṣya dvādaśa varṣāṇi puṣkare niyataḥ śuciḥ kratūn sarvān avāpnoti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: He who dwells at Puṣkara for twelve years with discipline and purity obtains the merit of all sacrifices and goes to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: yas tu varṣaśataṃ pūrṇam agnihotram upāsate kārttikīṃ vā vased ekāṃ puṣkare samam eva tat
english: But he who tends the Agnihotra fire for a full hundred years — to reside at Puṣkara for even a single Kārttikī night is equal to that.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ puṣkaraṃ gantuṃ duṣkaraṃ puṣkare tapaḥ duṣkaraṃ puṣkare dānaṃ vastuṃ caiva suduṣkaram
english: It is difficult to go to Puṣkara; difficult to perform austerity at Puṣkara; difficult to give charity at Puṣkara; and to reside there is very difficult indeed.

sanskrit: uṣya dvādaśarātraṃ tu niyato niyatāśanaḥ pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtto jambūmārgaṃ samāviśet
english: Having dwelt there for twelve nights with discipline and regulated eating, one should proceed, circumambulating as one goes, and enter the path of Jambū.

sanskrit: jambūmārgaṃ samāviśya devarṣipitṛsevitam aśvamedham avāpnoti viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Having entered the path of Jambū, frequented by gods, sages, and ancestors, one obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tatroṣya rajanīḥ pañca ṣaṣṭhakālakṣamī naraḥ na durgatim avāpnoti siddhiṃ prāpnoti cottamām
english: Having dwelt there for five nights, enduring until the sixth period, a man does not reach misfortune and attains the highest perfection.

sanskrit: jambūmārgād upāvṛtto gacchet taṇḍulikāśramam na durgatim avāpnoti svargaloke ca pūjyate
english: Having turned back from the path of Jambū, one should proceed to the hermitage of Taṇḍulika; he does not reach misfortune and is honoured in the celestial world.

sanskrit: agastyasara āsādya pitṛdevārcane rataḥ trirātropoṣito rājann agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Having reached the lake of Agastya, devoted to honouring ancestors and gods, and fasting for three nights, O king, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: śākavṛttiḥ phalair vāpi kaumāraṃ vindate padam kaṇvāśramaṃ samāsādya śrījuṣṭaṃ lokapūjitam
english: Living on vegetables or fruits alone, one attains the state of Kumāra; having reached the hermitage of Kaṇva, graced with prosperity and worshipped by the world —

sanskrit: dharmāraṇyaṃ hi tat puṇyaṃ ādyaṃ ca bharatarṣabha yatra praviṣṭamātro vai pāpebhyo vipramucyate
english: For that is the holy and primordial forest of righteousness, O bull of the Bhāratas, where one who has merely entered is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: arcayitvā pitṝn devān niyato niyatāśanaḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalam aśnute
english: Having worshipped the ancestors and the gods with discipline and regulated eating, one enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice rich in all desired things.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā yayātipatanaṃ vrajet hayamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti tatra vai
english: Having circumambulated it, one should then go to Yayātipātana; there one truly obtains the fruit of the Hayamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: mahākālaṃ tato gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ koṭitīrtham upaspṛśya hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: From there one should go to Mahākāla with discipline and regulated eating; having touched the Koṭi holy place, one obtains the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña puṇyasthānam umāpateḥ nāmnā bhadravaṭaṃ nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
english: From there, O knower of righteousness, one should go to the holy site of Umā's lord named Bhadravata, famous throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: tatrābhigamya ceśānaṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet mahādevaprasādāc ca gāṇapatyam avāpnuyāt
english: Having come there and worshipped Īśāna, one obtains the fruit of a gift of a thousand cows; and by the grace of Mahādeva, one attains the rank of chief of Gaṇas.

sanskrit: narmadām atha cāsādya nadīṃ trailokyaviśrutām tarpayitvā pitṝn devān agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then reaching the Narmadā, the river famous throughout the three worlds, having satisfied the ancestors and the gods, one obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ sindhum āsādya brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ agniṣṭomam avāpnoti vimānaṃ cādhirohati
english: Reaching the southern Sindhu as a celibate student with mastered senses, one obtains the merit of an Agniṣṭoma and ascends to a celestial chariot.
